items.title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
items.summary: Around 1,800 people were arrested after nationwide protests saw outbreaks of violence and vandalism.

items.title: Watch: Parisians wake up to protest damage and looted shops
items.summary: Violence broke out across France on Saturday during the latest day of demonstrations against conditions in schools and the cost of living.

items.title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion
items.summary: The Green Party leader said, while he wanted to amend it, the motion would stand until 2028.

items.title: Ending corridor care in hospitals for children will be a priority, says health secretary
items.summary: Yvette Cooper also announces £140m investment in England's urgent care system, ahead of winter.

items.title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
items.summary: BBC News hears from users, dealers, prison and recovery workers as the country battles with a deadly new drug epidemic.

items.title: Police officer in hospital after being shot in Nottingham
items.summary: A firearm has been recovered by officers after a man and a woman fled the scene, detectives say.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV thanks wellwishers in first event after cancer surgery
items.summary: The Pope's first event since his lung cancer diagnosis and surgery saw him recite the traditional Angelus prayer from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace.

items.title: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat
items.summary: Satellite images give clues about how Kim spends his holidays - something far out of reach for most North Koreans.
